definitions.gloss: to be cornered; to be driven into a corner; to be backed against the wall
definitions.explanation: To be put in a situation where there is no way out or no options left. Can refer to physical pursuit, psychological pressure, or being trapped by circumstances.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}は{追|お}い{詰|つ}められた。
{借金|しゃっきん}で{精神的|せいしんてき}に{追|お}い{詰|つ}められている。
examples.english: He is being mentally driven into a corner by debt.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}{終盤|しゅうばん}、{相手|あいて}チームに{追|お}い{詰|つ}められたが、なんとか{逆転|ぎゃくてん}した。
examples.english: We were cornered by the opposing team late in the game, but somehow managed to turn it around.

notes:
USAGE:
The passive form of {追|お}い{詰|つ}める (to corner, to drive into a corner). Often used to describe situations where someone has run out of options due to external pressure — financial problems, workplace stress, competitive situations, or being chased. Can be used both literally (physical pursuit) and figuratively (psychological/situational pressure).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {精神的|せいしんてき}に{追|お}い{詰|つ}められる (to be mentally cornered)
- {窮地|きゅうち}に{追|お}い{詰|つ}められる (to be driven into a tight spot)
- {崖|がけ}っぷちに{追|お}い{詰|つ}められる (to be pushed to the edge of a cliff)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {窮地|きゅうち}に{立|た}たされる: to be placed in a predicament — similar but more formal
- {行|い}き{詰|づ}まる: to reach a dead end — implies being stuck rather than pressured by others
